doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Advice to aspiring jazz musicians
summary: Only do it if you have passion; he talks to schools and notes the highs and the down time.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I don’t know. Well it’s been a real pleasure talking to you.
If you had an acquaintance, let’s say a nephew or something like that who was an aspiring jazz musician, and said I really want to do this for a living, what would you honestly say to that person?

Well I’ve gone into schools quite a lot. I have a little thing that I call Jazz and the Real Jam. And I go in and talk about the music and I play and I show them how it’s done, and the basic terms. I always say unless you have the passion, unless it’s something you just absolutely must do, don’t. And I mean that. Because you have to have that fire in your gut, otherwise the business will destroy you.
Yeah. I can’t recall who it was, but someone said that jazz is like having an illness. You really have to do it.
Yeah. And the highs are like nothing else you’ll ever know, but enjoy those, there’s an awful lot of time that’s down time.
